subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Wuyi Rock Tea
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Wuyi Rock Tea.

hook.text: Wuyi Mountain teas are called 'rock teas' because the plants grow in crevices between ancient sandstone cliffs.

buildup.text: Thin, mineral-rich soil forces deep root systems. Mist and shade from canyon walls protect the delicate leaves.

discovery.text: The result is 'yan yun'—rock rhyme—a mineral taste sensation unique to Wuyi teas that lingers in the mouth.

twist.text: Da Hong Pao (Big Red Robe) from the original six bushes is the most expensive tea ever sold—over $1M per kilogram.

climax.text: Those original bushes are now government-protected. All commercial Da Hong Pao comes from cuttings and grafts.

punchline.text: Rock, mist, centuries of roots. Wuyi teas taste like geology.

quiz.question: What is 'yan yun' in Wuyi rock teas?
options: A mineral taste sensation unique to rock-grown teas
